title: Beatrix and the Winter
premise: Zephyrine Ravensworth returns to the family house in Hollowmere to bury their twin Beatrix, only to find the funeral arrangements already made, the will already signed, and a childhood imaginary friend named Wren waiting on the porch, unchanged after twenty years. As the town's grief curdles into something hungrier, Zephyrine realizes the thing being buried isn't Beatrix—and that the 'last resident' of the house is a title passed down through signatures, not blood. To survive until sunrise and expose what was invited in generations ago, Zephyrine must stop being invisible, claim an identity no one gave them, and burn the inheritance before dawn—ending with Zephyrine signing nothing, walking out as the sun rises over an empty grave.
about_author: Odile Nystrom is the pen name of a former probate clerk from coastal Maine who spent a decade reading other people's final wishes before writing her own. Her work explores the horror hidden in paperwork, inheritance, and small towns that remember too much.

chapters.title: The Wrong Sibling
chapters.summary: Zephyrine arrives in Hollowmere by night bus for Beatrix's funeral, carrying guilt over twenty years of silence. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: dread disguised as obligation; the town greets them with unsettling warmth, calling them by Beatrix's name.

chapters.title: Papers Already Signed
chapters.summary: At the house, Zephyrine finds the funeral fully arranged, the death certificate filed, and a will bearing Beatrix's signature dated three days before she died. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: creeping wrongness—the machinery of death ran ahead of the death itself.

chapters.title: Wren on the Porch
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's childhood imaginary friend sits on the porch swing, unchanged, adult-sized but wearing the same coat. Wren says they've been waiting to be seen again. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: terror braided with longing; the first crack in Zephyrine's disbelief.

chapters.title: Open Casket, Closed Case
chapters.summary: At the viewing, the body is wrong—too tall, hands too smooth. The undertaker, Mrs. Calloway, watches Zephyrine too closely. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: grief colliding with certainty that this corpse is not their twin.

chapters.title: What the Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Zephyrine interviews neighbors; each describes Beatrix differently, and each description matches Zephyrine instead. Old Mr. Vetch mentions 'the last resident' like a job title. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: identity dissolving; the town can't tell the twins apart because it never could.

chapters.title: The House Counts Its Rooms
chapters.summary: Zephyrine maps the house and finds one room more than the blueprints allow—a door that appears only when unobserved. Wren refuses to enter it. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: claustrophobic escalation; home becomes hostile architecture.

chapters.title: Beatrix's Letters
chapters.summary: In Beatrix's room, Zephyrine finds letters written in their own handwriting, describing events Zephyrine never lived. One letter says: 'Don't sign anything.' POV: alternating Zephyrine and letter-voice. Emotional beat: vertigo—who has been living whose life?

chapters.title: Invited In
chapters.summary: Wren finally explains: the house requires a resident who consents, and every generation someone signs. The Ravensworths have been feeding it names for two hundred years. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: revelation with tenderness; Wren was created as a witness, not a friend.

chapters.title: Mrs. Calloway's Ledger
chapters.summary: Zephyrine breaks into the funeral parlor and finds a ledger of residents dating to 1798—each entry signed, each followed by a date of 'retirement.' Beatrix's name is already entered. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: cold fury; justice here lives outside any law.

chapters.title: The Town That Signs
chapters.summary: Hollowmere holds a 'welcome supper' where everyone urges Zephyrine to finalize the estate. Refusing feels physically dangerous; the walls of the house lean closer each hour. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: social horror; politeness as predation.

chapters.title: Vetch's Confession
chapters.summary: Dying Mr. Vetch admits he was meant to be last resident forty years ago but tricked a Ravensworth into signing instead. He begs Zephyrine to break the chain before he dies and the house comes collecting. POV: Vetch. Emotional beat: pitiable cowardice; corruption inherited like property.

chapters.title: The Room Opens
chapters.summary: The extra door stands open at midnight. Inside: every object Zephyrine has ever lost, including childhood drawings of Wren—and a contract with Zephyrine's name pre-filled. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: seduction; the house offers belonging in exchange for selfhood.

chapters.title: Which Twin
chapters.summary: A figure claiming to be Beatrix appears, insisting Zephyrine died years ago and they've been dead all along. The evidence is damning. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: identity crisis at its nadir; belief versus refusal.

chapters.title: Wren's True Name
chapters.summary: Wren reveals they were the first resident's imaginary friend, bound as witness when the first signature was given. They can testify—but only if someone sees them, truly, which costs the seer their invisibility forever. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered; love as exposure.

chapters.title: Sunset Deadline
chapters.summary: Calloway presents final papers at dusk: sign by sunrise or the house chooses its own resident. The town gathers outside, patient and smiling. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: siege begins; the long night starts.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: Hours of pressure: phone calls in Beatrix's voice, doors that lead to Zephyrine's happiest memories, the contract rewriting itself more generously each time it's refused. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: attrition; temptation refined into torture.

chapters.title: What Was Invited In
chapters.summary: Reading the original 1798 contract, Zephyrine learns the family didn't summon the house—they invited it to punish an injustice, and it corrupted its mandate into appetite. Justice became the monster. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: thematic climax of understanding; power corrupting purpose.

chapters.title: Beatrix, Really
chapters.summary: The false Beatrix falters and admits it's the house wearing her shape—but in doing so reveals where the real Beatrix's body lies beneath the floor of the extra room. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: rage crystallizing into resolve; grief weaponized.

chapters.title: Witness
chapters.summary: Zephyrine looks at Wren—fully, deliberately—and speaks their testimony aloud: naming every signer, every victim, every theft. The ledger burns itself blank. POV: dual Zephyrine/Wren. Emotional beat: catharsis; visibility chosen over safety.

chapters.title: The House Objects
chapters.summary: The house fights back, flooding halls with memory, offering Zephyrine a life where Beatrix lived. Zephyrine walks through it toward the hearth where the original contract sleeps inside the chimney. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: endurance; refusing the kindest lie.

chapters.title: Burn Before Sunrise
chapters.summary: As the sky lightens, Zephyrine burns the founding contract in the hearth while the house screams in every voice it has stolen. Wren holds the door open—not as resident, but as witness released. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: climax; destruction as liberation.

chapters.title: Nothing Signed
chapters.summary: Dawn. The extra room is gone, the ledger ash, the grave empty because there was never a body. Zephyrine leaves Hollowmere on foot beside Wren, unnamed on no register, finally visible and finally free. POV: Zephyrine. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; identity claimed, not assigned.
